Job Description

Business Title:
Indicators Economic Data Analyst

Exemption: Exempt

Work Schedule

Work Schedule: Hybrid work arrangement with at least 2 days per week on-site.

Budgeted Salary

$91,644-$123,000

School/Unit Description

The Stanford Digital Economy Lab conducts groundbreaking research on the impact of the digital economy. We bring together an interdisciplinary group of researchers to study how digital technologies are transforming work, organizations, and the economy. Our insights help companies, policymakers, students, and professionals respond to the opportunities and challenges created by digitization. The Lab is part of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence and is co-sponsored by the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research.

Position Summary

The Stanford Digital Economy Lab is seeking an Economic Data Analyst to perform complex technical and analytical work supporting Indicators , the Lab’s public-facing platform for measuring the economic impact of artificial intelligence. Reporting to the Research Manager for Indicators, this position will query and integrate structured economic and labor-market data, independently produce standard and custom reports, devise methods for identifying patterns and trends, build non-routine analytical databases, and create publication-ready metrics and visualizations with minimal supervision.

The Economic Data Analyst will clean, validate, integrate, and document data from sources including ADP, the U.S. Census Bureau, job-posting providers, government agencies, surveys, and public repositories. The analyst will create analysis-ready relational tables, longitudinal datasets, derived indicators, data dictionaries, quality-control summaries, reports, charts, dashboards, and approved data extracts. The position will also develop and evaluate algorithms and statistical models related to AI adoption and exposure, employment, wages, occupations, industries, and skills demand; recommend improvements to data collection and reporting; respond to non-routine analytical and survey requests; implement data standards and common metric definitions; and test prototype pipelines, APIs, calculations, database changes, and visualizations for release readiness.

The successful candidate will work closely with economists, faculty, research scientists, postdoctoral scholars, graduate research assistants, data providers, engineers, designers, communications teams, and other Stanford partners. The role requires strong technical judgment, careful documentation, and the ability to translate complex findings into trustworthy information for academic, policy, industry, media, and public audiences.

This fixed-term position (3 years, renewable)

Preferred/Desired Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and three years of relevant experience, or a combination of education and relevant experience, in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics, computer science, data science, or engineering.

Strong SQL and Python skills; experience with R, cloud environments such as Google Cloud, Git-based version control, APIs, and visualization or business-intelligence tools is preferred.
Experience working with large economic or labor-market datasets, including restricted, licensed, or confidential data.
Knowledge of econometrics, data analysis, data visualization, reproducible research, and artificial intelligence measurement.
Excellent analytical, organizational, written, and oral communication skills; ability to complete detailed work accurately under deadlines with minimal supervision.
Creative, independent problem-solving skills and the ability to collaborate with researchers and technical partners from diverse backgrounds.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Evaluate and develop new or modifications of usable data from complex data sources. Assess and produce relevant, standard, or custom information (reports, charts, graphs, and tables) from structured data sources by querying data repositories and generating the associated information.
Devise methods for identifying patterns and trends in available information sources using a variety of qualitative and quantitative techniques. Determine and recommend additional data collection and reporting requirements.
Design and customize reports based on data in the database. Distribute and disseminate reports to applicable agencies, researchers, management, and other internal end-users.
Create non-routine databases and generate related information summaries.
Perform statistical analyses appropriate to complex data and reporting requirements.
Serve as a resource for non-routine inquiries such as requests for statistics or surveys.
Lead the implementation of data standards and common data elements for data collection.
Collaborate with technical staff to standardize and systemize routine reports, dashboards, and metrics.
May test prototype software and participate in the approval and release process for new software.

Minimum Education

Bachelor’s degree.

Minimum Experience

Three years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience. Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics, or engineering.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

In-depth knowledge and experience using and applying analytical software, database management system software, database reporting software, database user interface and query software, and data mining software.
Demonstrated ability to collect data using a variety of methods, such as data mining and hardcopy or electronic documentation study, to improve or expand databases.
Intermediate statistical ability.
Strong listening, verbal, and written communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple activities in a deadline-oriented environment; highly organized, flexible, and rigorous attention to detail.
Ability to use logic to calculate data; efficiently construct a database or scrutinize the form of a question.
Ability to work with data of varying levels of quality and validity.
Demonstrated ability to produce data in a clear and understandable manner meeting user requirements.
Ability to work effectively with multiple internal and external customers.
Ability to take a leadership role on projects and with users/clients.

Overview

The Integrated Operations Support Division (IOSD) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) seeks a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Specialist to serve as the functional system administrator for ArcGIS Enterprise, and partners with IT staff and data owners across ORNL. The GIS Specialist is the primary point of contact for the enterprise GIS platform, fostering customer relationships by proactively identifying, implementing, and communicating continuous improvement efforts.

The GIS Specialist will build awareness of existing GIS capabilities, develop, and implement new tools and workflows, and support the vision, roadmap, standards, and governance for GIS across the Directorate. Supported functional areas include site, facility, and asset management, utilities distribution, logistics, environmental safety & health, strategic planning, construction, engineering, emergency management, and security.

Major Duties/Responsibilities

Serve as the functional system administrator for ArcGIS Enterprise (Portal, Server, Data Store) and associated applications and datasets.
Design, develop, and maintain web maps, web applications, web scenes, dashboards, and mobile apps using ArcGIS Experience Builder, Dashboards, Survey123, and related tools.
Administer and optimize enterprise geodatabases, including SQL views, schema design, privileges, versioning, and replica management.
Support data interoperability efforts to integrate CAD, BIM, tabular, and other datasets into enterprise GIS; ensure correct coordinate systems and projections (including ORNL custom coordinates).
Develop and maintain Python scripts, Arcade expressions, attribute rules, and automated processes (including batch scripts and Windows Task Scheduler jobs).
Publish and manage map, feature, image, geoprocessing, and real-time (GeoEvent) services.
Implement and support offline GIS workflows, mobile field work, GPS-based data collection, and road network analysis (Network Analyst).
Maintain data governance, metadata standards, and documentation for Enterprise GIS assets.
Develop and maintain GIS platform documentation including Software Quality Assurance, Business Impact Analysis, Contingency Planning, System Security Plans, etc.
Work closely with managers, process owners, IT staff, and end users to understand requirements, prioritize enhancements, and implement system/process improvements.
Provide general troubleshooting and user support to both GIS technical staff and non-technical map users
Administer licensing and user accounts for desktop and server applications.
Coordinate software procurement, planning, installation and vendor relations and support including training, coordinating software demonstrations, benchmarking, etc.
Deliver ORNL’s mission by aligning behaviors, priorities, and interactions with our core values of Impact, Integrity, Teamwork, Safety, and Service. Promote equal opportunity by fostering a respectful workplace – in how we treat one another, work together, and measure success.

Basic Qualifications

A BS/BA degree in GIS, geography, environmental science, environmental informatics, computer science, engineering, natural sciences, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of relevant GIS experience.
Proficient with ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Enterprise; capable of architecting, developing, and maintaining web maps and web applications from enterprise data.
Experience with GIS data analysis, data cleaning/curation, and integration of multiple data formats (including CAD).
Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases for GIS workflows.

Preferred Qualifications

MS/MA degree in geography, GIS, environmental science, environmental informatics, computer science, engineering, natural sciences, or a related field.
Experience as a technical lead, system administrator, or architect for an enterprise GIS environment.
Experience working with facilities and operations organizations, city/county governments, or utilities.
Advanced experience with:
ArcGIS Experience Builder and Dashboards
Enterprise geodatabases (e.g., SQL Server) including versioning and replicas
ArcGIS Server and Portal administration
Network Analyst and road network management
GeoEvent Manager and real-time GIS

Experience integrating GIS with asset management systems (e.g., Octave EAM) or other enterprise business systems.
Experience with Python and/or Arcade for GIS automation, analysis, or business logic.
Background in software support or customer-facing technical roles, including training and documentation.
Ability to work collaboratively with a diverse group of stakeholders and contribute to team goals.
Strong prioritization, communication, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail.

Special Requirements

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain an HSPD-12 PIV badge.

For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.

To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

For Hybrid Eligible Positions

This position is located in Oak Ridge, Tennessee and requires onsite presence. We offer a flexible work environment that supports both the organization and the employee. A hybrid/onsite working arrangement may be available with this position, which provides flexibility to work periodically from your home, while reporting onsite to the Oak Ridge, Tennessee location on a weekly and regular basis.

About ORNL

As a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science national laboratory, ORNL has an impressive 80-year legacy of addressing the nation’s most pressing challenges. Our team is made up of over 7,000 dedicated and innovative individuals! Our goal is to create an environment where a variety of perspectives and backgrounds are valued, ensuring ORNL is known as a top choice for employment. These principles are essential for supporting our broader mission to drive scientific breakthroughs and translate them into solutions for energy, environmental, and security challenges facing the nation.

ORNL offers competitive pay and benefits programs to attract and retain individuals who demonstrate exceptional work behaviors. The laboratory provides a range of employee benefits, including medical and retirement plans and flexible work hours, to support the well-being of you and your family. Employee amenities such as on-site fitness, banking, and cafeteria facilities are also available for added convenience.

Other benefits include the following: Prescription Drug Plan, Dental Plan, Vision Plan, 401(k) Retirement Plan, Contributory Pension Plan, Life Insurance, Disability Benefits, Generous Vacation and Holidays, Parental Leave, Legal Insurance with Identity Theft Protection, Employee Assistance Plan, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, Wellness Programs, Educational Assistance, Relocation Assistance, and Employee Discounts.
